title: Continuation vs Discontinuation of Renin-Angiotensin System Inhibitors Before Major Noncardiac Surgery: The Stop-or-Not Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Legrand M, Falcone J, Cholley B, Charbonneau H, Delaporte A, Lemoine A, et al.; Stop-or-Not Trial Group
population: Patients treated with an ACE inhibitor (46%) or angiotensin receptor blocker (54%) for at least 3 months and scheduled for major noncardiac surgery at 40 hospitals in France, 2018 to 2023; mean age 67 years, 65% men
funder: This study was supported by a grant from the French Ministry of Health (Programme Hospitalier de Recherche Clinique National). The French Ministry of Health had no role in the design and conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; and decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
authorConflicts: Several authors report personal fees from device and drug companies, among them Viatris, Alexion, La Jolla, Edwards Lifesciences, Becton Dickinson, Vifor Pharma, Pfizer, Medtronic, Baxter, Abbott and General Electric.
result: Continuation until the day of surgery (n=1107) against discontinuation 48 hours before surgery (n=1115). Death from any cause or major postoperative complications within 28 days: 247 of 1107 (22%) with continuation against 245 of 1115 (22%) with discontinuation (risk ratio 1.02, 95% CI 0.87 to 1.19). Intraoperative hypotension occurred in 54% with continuation against 41% with discontinuation (risk ratio 1.31, 1.19 to 1.44). Acute kidney injury, organ failure and length of stay did not differ.
